The circuit implements a 12-cell 1D Cellular Automaton with periodic boundary conditions (a ring of 12 flip-flops). Each block of gates calculates the next state of cell `c[i]` based on its own state and its neighbors `c[i-1]` and `c[i+1]` (with indices wrapping around modulo 12).
Tracing the NAND gates for any bit `i`:
- `nm[i] = ~c[i]`
- `nr[i] = ~c[i+1]`
- `or[i] = ~(~c[i] & ~c[i+1]) = c[i] | c[i+1]`
- `t1_[i] = ~(c[i-1] & (c[i] | c[i+1]))`
- `t2_[i] = ~(c[i-1] & t1_[i]) = ~c[i-1] | (c[i] | c[i+1])`
- `t3_[i] = ~((c[i] | c[i+1]) & t1_[i]) = ~(c[i] | c[i+1]) | c[i-1]`
- `x[i] = ~(t2_[i] & t3_[i]) = c[i-1] ^ (c[i] | c[i+1])`

The next state of each flip-flop is determined by `Left XOR (Center OR Right)`, which is exactly the logic for **Rule 30**.
